note: Phase 3 curated question bank. SERVER-OWNED. correct_options / correct_bool are NEVER sent to the client before submission (see agent/assessment_bank.py public views). Types: single (one correct), multi (exact set), tf (true/false). marks default 1. concept_ids map into agent/data/assessment_concepts.json. Options are referenced by stable letter ids so answer randomization can shuffle display order without changing identity.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of accessing an element by index in an array?
questions.explanation: Arrays store elements contiguously, so an index maps directly to a memory offset — constant time.

questions.prompt: Which data structure follows Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) ordering?
questions.explanation: A stack pushes and pops from the same end, so the last item pushed is the first popped (LIFO).

questions.prompt: Binary search requires the input array to be sorted.
questions.explanation: Binary search relies on ordering to discard half the range each step; on unsorted data it is incorrect.

questions.prompt: What is the average-case time complexity of quicksort?
questions.explanation: Quicksort averages O(n log n); its worst case is O(n^2) with poor pivots.

questions.prompt: In a balanced binary search tree with n nodes, what is the time complexity of a search?
questions.explanation: A balanced BST has height O(log n), so search follows one root-to-leaf path in O(log n).

questions.prompt: Which of the following are graph traversal algorithms? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: BFS, DFS and Dijkstra all traverse graphs. Binary search operates on a sorted linear sequence, not a graph.

questions.prompt: A hash table lookup is O(1) on average. What is its worst-case lookup complexity?
questions.explanation: With many collisions in one bucket, a lookup may scan all n entries — O(n) worst case.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of inserting at the head of a singly linked list (given the head pointer)?
questions.explanation: Head insertion rewires a constant number of pointers regardless of list length — O(1).

questions.prompt: Which structure follows First-In-First-Out (FIFO) ordering?
questions.explanation: A queue enqueues at the rear and dequeues from the front, so the first item in is the first out (FIFO).

questions.prompt: Which sorting algorithms have O(n log n) worst-case time complexity? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Merge sort and heap sort guarantee O(n log n). Quicksort's worst case is O(n^2); bubble sort is O(n^2).

questions.prompt: Which keyword is used to define a constant (unchangeable) variable in Java?
questions.explanation: `final` prevents reassignment. `const` is a reserved but unused keyword in Java.

questions.prompt: In Java, `int` is an object type.
questions.explanation: `int` is a primitive type. Its object wrapper is `Integer`.

questions.prompt: Which concept allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method already defined in its superclass?
questions.explanation: Overriding replaces the superclass method with the same signature. Overloading differs by parameter list.

questions.prompt: Which Java collection does NOT allow duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: A Set stores unique elements; HashSet rejects duplicates. The List types permit duplicates.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are valid access modifiers in Java? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Java has public, private, protected and package-private (default). `internal` is C#, not Java.

questions.prompt: Which exception is checked at compile time in Java?
questions.explanation: IOException is a checked exception (must be declared/caught). The others are unchecked RuntimeExceptions.

questions.prompt: In Java, which component reclaims memory occupied by unreachable objects?
questions.explanation: The JVM garbage collector automatically frees unreachable objects; Java has no manual free().

questions.prompt: What is the entry-point method signature of a Java application?
questions.explanation: The JVM invokes `public static void main(String[] args)`.

questions.prompt: A Java `HashMap` guarantees the iteration order of its keys.
questions.explanation: HashMap gives no ordering guarantee. LinkedHashMap preserves insertion order; TreeMap sorts keys.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Java interfaces (Java 8+) are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: An interface can declare default methods with a body
A class can implement multiple interfaces
Interface fields are instance variables by default

questions.explanation: Interfaces support default and static methods and multiple inheritance of type. Interface fields are implicitly public static final constants, not instance variables.

questions.prompt: Which Python data structure is ordered and mutable?
questions.explanation: Lists are ordered and mutable. Tuples and strings are immutable; frozensets are unordered and immutable.

questions.prompt: What does the expression `type(3 / 2)` evaluate to in Python 3?
questions.explanation: In Python 3, `/` is true division and always returns a float; `//` is floor division.

questions.prompt: Python strings are immutable.
questions.explanation: String methods return new strings; the original object is never modified in place.

questions.prompt: Why is using a mutable object like [] as a default argument value considered a pitfall?

options.text: The default is created once and shared across all calls
It is slower than using None

questions.explanation: Default values are evaluated once at definition time, so a mutable default persists mutations across calls.

questions.prompt: Which Python structure stores unique, unordered elements?
questions.explanation: A set holds unique elements with no defined order.

questions.prompt: Which of the following Python types are immutable? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Tuples, strings and frozensets are immutable. Lists are mutable.

questions.prompt: What does a Python generator function use to yield values lazily?
questions.explanation: `yield` produces a value and suspends the generator, resuming on the next iteration.

questions.prompt: What is the output of `len({1, 1, 2, 3, 3})` in Python?
questions.explanation: A set literal removes duplicates, leaving {1, 2, 3} with length 3.

questions.prompt: Which operator performs integer (floor) division in Python?
questions.explanation: `//` is floor division; `/` is true division; `%` is modulo; `**` is exponentiation.

questions.prompt: In Python, `is` compares object identity, while `==` compares value equality.
questions.explanation: `is` tests whether two names refer to the same object; `==` tests equal values via __eq__.

questions.prompt: Which format specifier prints an integer with printf in C?
questions.explanation: %d prints a signed decimal integer; %s is string, %f is float, %c is char.

questions.prompt: In C, array indices start at 0.
questions.explanation: C arrays are zero-indexed; the first element is a[0].

questions.prompt: What does the `&` operator return when applied to a variable in C?
questions.explanation: `&x` yields the memory address of x; `*p` dereferences a pointer to the value.

questions.prompt: Which function dynamically allocates uninitialized memory on the heap in C?
questions.explanation: malloc allocates uninitialized memory; calloc zero-initializes; `new` is C++.

questions.prompt: What is the result of using memory after it has been freed with free() in C?
questions.explanation: Use-after-free is undefined behavior in C — it may crash, corrupt data, or appear to work.

questions.prompt: Which storage-class specifier gives a local variable a lifetime spanning the whole program in C?
questions.explanation: A `static` local variable persists for the program's lifetime while keeping local scope.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are handled by the C preprocessor? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: #include, #define and #ifdef are preprocessor directives. sizeof is a compile-time operator, not a preprocessor directive.

questions.prompt: What is the size of a `char` in C, as guaranteed by the standard?
questions.explanation: sizeof(char) is always 1 by definition in C.

questions.prompt: Which operator is used for dynamic memory allocation in C++?
questions.explanation: C++ uses `new`/`delete`; `new` also calls the constructor, unlike malloc.

questions.prompt: In C++, `delete` should be used to free memory allocated with `new`.
questions.explanation: Memory from `new` is freed with `delete` (and `new[]` with `delete[]`).

questions.prompt: Which C++ feature enables writing a single function or class that works with multiple types?
questions.explanation: Templates provide compile-time generic programming over types.

questions.prompt: What keyword declares a method that can be overridden and dispatched at runtime in C++?
questions.explanation: `virtual` enables dynamic (runtime) dispatch through a base-class pointer or reference.

questions.prompt: Which C++ smart pointer enforces unique ownership of a resource?
questions.explanation: unique_ptr is non-copyable and owns its resource exclusively; shared_ptr is reference-counted.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are C++ STL container types? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: vector, map and array are STL containers. printf is a C I/O function, not a container.

questions.prompt: C++ supports multiple inheritance from more than one base class.
questions.explanation: Unlike Java, C++ allows a class to inherit from multiple base classes.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk of a base class with virtual methods but a non-virtual destructor when deleting via a base pointer?

options.text: The derived destructor may not run, leaking resources

questions.explanation: Deleting a derived object through a base pointer with a non-virtual destructor is undefined behavior and typically skips the derived destructor.

questions.prompt: What uniquely identifies each row in a relational table?
questions.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies each row and cannot be null.

questions.prompt: A foreign key can reference the primary key of another table.
questions.explanation: A foreign key enforces referential integrity by referencing a key in another (or the same) table.

questions.prompt: Which normal form eliminates partial dependency of non-key attributes on a composite primary key?
questions.explanation: 2NF removes partial dependencies on part of a composite key (after 1NF).

questions.prompt: Which properties make up the ACID guarantees of a transaction? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and Durability — all four.

questions.prompt: What is a primary trade-off of adding an index to a frequently-written table?

options.text: Writes incur extra cost to maintain the index

questions.explanation: An index speeds up matching reads but adds maintenance overhead and storage on inserts/updates/deletes.

questions.prompt: Which isolation issue occurs when a transaction reads data later rolled back by another?
questions.explanation: A dirty read reads uncommitted data that may be rolled back.

questions.prompt: Denormalization can improve read performance at the cost of data redundancy.
questions.explanation: Denormalization trades redundancy and update anomalies for fewer joins and faster reads.

questions.prompt: Which language subset defines database schema objects such as tables?
questions.explanation: DDL (Data Definition Language) defines schema (CREATE/ALTER/DROP); DML manipulates data.

questions.prompt: Which SQL clause filters rows before grouping?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before aggregation; HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

questions.prompt: Which JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right, with NULLs where there is no match?
questions.explanation: A LEFT JOIN keeps every left-table row, filling unmatched right columns with NULL.

questions.prompt: Which clause filters groups after a GROUP BY aggregation?
questions.explanation: HAVING applies conditions to aggregated groups; WHERE cannot reference aggregates.

questions.prompt: Which aggregate function counts the number of rows?
questions.explanation: COUNT() returns the number of rows (or non-null values of a column).

questions.prompt: Which of the following are SQL DDL statements? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: CREATE, ALTER and DROP are DDL. SELECT is DML (query).

questions.prompt: The SQL `DISTINCT` keyword removes duplicate rows from a result set.
questions.explanation: DISTINCT returns only unique rows across the selected columns.

questions.prompt: In a query with GROUP BY, which columns may appear unaggregated in the SELECT list (standard SQL)?

options.text: Only columns in the GROUP BY

questions.explanation: Standard SQL requires non-aggregated SELECT columns to appear in the GROUP BY clause.

questions.prompt: Which SQL statement retrieves data from a table?
questions.explanation: SELECT is the SQL query statement for retrieving rows.

questions.prompt: What is a process?
questions.explanation: A process is an instance of a program in execution, with its own address space.

questions.prompt: Threads of the same process share the same address space.
questions.explanation: Threads within a process share code, heap and global data, but each has its own stack.

questions.prompt: Which CPU scheduling algorithm can cause starvation of long processes if short jobs keep arriving?
questions.explanation: SJF favors short jobs, so a steady stream of them can starve long jobs.

questions.prompt: What is thrashing in an operating system?
questions.explanation: Thrashing is when the system spends more time paging than executing due to insufficient memory.

questions.prompt: Which conditions must ALL hold for a deadlock (Coffman conditions)? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Deadlock needs mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, NO preemption, and circular wait. 'Preemption allowed' breaks deadlock, so it is not a condition.

questions.prompt: Which synchronization primitive allows up to N concurrent accesses to a resource?
questions.explanation: A counting semaphore permits up to its initial count of concurrent holders; a mutex/binary semaphore permits one.

questions.prompt: Virtual memory primarily allows a system to do what?

options.text: Run programs larger than physical RAM
Eliminate the need for a disk

questions.explanation: Virtual memory uses disk-backed paging so a process can use an address space larger than physical RAM.

questions.prompt: Which scheduling algorithm gives each process a fixed time slice in turn?
questions.explanation: Round Robin assigns each process a fixed quantum cyclically, improving responsiveness.

questions.prompt: How many layers does the OSI reference model have?
questions.explanation: The OSI model has 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

questions.prompt: TCP provides reliable, connection-oriented delivery.
questions.explanation: TCP uses handshakes, sequencing, acknowledgements and retransmission for reliable, ordered delivery.

questions.prompt: Which transport protocol is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery?
questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless and best-effort — no handshakes, ordering or retransmission.

questions.prompt: Which protocol resolves domain names to IP addresses?
questions.explanation: DNS maps human-readable domain names to IP addresses.

questions.prompt: How many bits are in an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits (four octets). IPv6 addresses are 128 bits.

questions.prompt: Which of the following protocols operate at the application layer? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: HTTP, SMTP and DNS are application-layer protocols. TCP is a transport-layer protocol.

questions.prompt: Which protocol dynamically assigns IP addresses to hosts on a network?
questions.explanation: DHCP automatically leases IP configuration (address, gateway, DNS) to hosts.

questions.prompt: Which port does HTTPS use by default?
questions.explanation: HTTPS defaults to port 443; plain HTTP uses 80.

questions.prompt: Which OOP principle hides internal state and exposes behavior through methods?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data with methods and restricts direct access to internal state.

questions.prompt: Inheritance lets a class acquire properties and behavior from another class.
questions.explanation: A subclass inherits fields and methods from its superclass, enabling reuse and specialization.

questions.prompt: Which principle allows objects of different classes to be treated through a common interface?
questions.explanation: Polymorphism lets a common interface invoke behavior specific to the actual object type.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are core principles of object-oriented programming? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism (and abstraction) are OOP pillars. Recursion is a general technique, not an OOP principle.

questions.prompt: What is an abstract class?

options.text: A class that cannot be instantiated directly
A class that is always final
A class with only static members

questions.explanation: An abstract class cannot be instantiated on its own; it serves as a base, often with abstract methods.

questions.prompt: Method overloading is an example of compile-time (static) polymorphism.
questions.explanation: Overloading is resolved at compile time by signature; overriding is runtime (dynamic) polymorphism.

questions.prompt: What is the decimal value of the binary number 1010?
Cache memory is faster but smaller than main memory (RAM).
questions.explanation: Cache sits closer to the CPU, is faster and more expensive per byte, and therefore smaller than RAM.

questions.prompt: Which sequence correctly describes the basic instruction cycle?
questions.explanation: The CPU fetches an instruction, decodes it, then executes it.

questions.prompt: In the memory hierarchy, which is typically the FASTEST?
questions.explanation: Registers are the fastest and smallest storage, directly inside the CPU.

questions.prompt: How is a negative integer most commonly represented in modern CPUs?
questions.explanation: Two's complement is standard: it has a single zero and lets addition/subtraction use the same hardware.

questions.prompt: What does pipelining in a CPU improve?
questions.explanation: Pipelining overlaps the execution stages of successive instructions, increasing throughput.

questions.prompt: Which SDLC model proceeds strictly sequentially through fixed phases?
questions.explanation: The Waterfall model flows one direction through sequential phases with little iteration.

questions.prompt: Unit testing verifies the behavior of individual components in isolation.
questions.explanation: Unit tests exercise the smallest testable parts (functions/classes) independently.

questions.prompt: Which testing level verifies that independently developed modules work together?
questions.explanation: Integration testing checks the interaction between combined modules.

questions.prompt: Which methodology emphasizes iterative delivery and responding to change?
questions.explanation: Agile delivers working software iteratively and adapts to changing requirements.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are SOLID design principles? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: SOLID = Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion. DRY is a separate principle.

questions.prompt: What does 'coupling' measure in software design?

options.text: The degree of interdependence between modules
The number of lines of code

questions.explanation: Coupling measures how dependent modules are on each other; low coupling is generally desirable.

questions.prompt: Which operation on a dynamic array is amortized O(1)?
questions.explanation: Appending is amortized O(1) thanks to geometric resizing; front operations are O(n) due to shifting.

questions.prompt: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits nodes in ascending sorted order?
questions.explanation: In-order traversal of a BST (left, node, right) yields keys in ascending order.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a Java primitive type?
questions.explanation: String is a class, not a primitive. int, boolean and double are primitives.

questions.prompt: Which interface does ArrayList implement?
questions.explanation: ArrayList implements the List interface (ordered, index-accessible, allows duplicates).

questions.prompt: Which Python literal creates a dictionary?
questions.explanation: {} creates an empty dict; [] is a list, () a tuple, and set() an empty set.

questions.prompt: What does a Python decorator do?

options.text: Wraps a function to extend or modify its behavior

questions.explanation: A decorator is a callable that takes a function and returns a (usually wrapped) function, applied with @syntax.

questions.prompt: What is the value of an uninitialized local (automatic) variable in C?
questions.explanation: Automatic variables are not zero-initialized; reading them before assignment gives indeterminate values.

questions.prompt: In C, an array name used in an expression typically decays to a pointer to its first element.
questions.explanation: Except with sizeof and &, an array name decays to a pointer to element 0.

questions.prompt: Which stream object is used for standard output in C++?
questions.explanation: std::cout is the standard output stream; std::cin is input, std::cerr is error output.

questions.prompt: Which STL container provides O(1) average lookup by key?
questions.explanation: unordered_map is hash-based with average O(1) lookup; std::map/set are tree-based O(log n).

questions.prompt: What is a candidate key?

options.text: A minimal set of attributes that uniquely identifies a row

questions.explanation: A candidate key is a minimal superkey; one candidate key is chosen as the primary key.

questions.prompt: Which index structure is most common for range queries in relational databases?
questions.explanation: B-tree indexes keep keys sorted, supporting efficient range scans; hash indexes support only equality.

questions.prompt: Which SQL constraint guarantees a column's values are unique AND not null?
questions.explanation: PRIMARY KEY implies both UNIQUE and NOT NULL. UNIQUE alone allows a null (per SQL standard).

questions.prompt: What does a correlated subquery depend on?

options.text: A value from the outer query, re-evaluated per outer row

questions.explanation: A correlated subquery references columns from the outer query and is logically re-evaluated for each outer row.

questions.prompt: Which system call creates a new process in UNIX by duplicating the caller?
questions.explanation: fork() creates a child process as a copy of the parent; exec() then replaces the image.

questions.prompt: A page fault occurs when:

options.text: A referenced page is not in physical memory

questions.explanation: A page fault traps to the OS when a referenced virtual page is not resident in RAM, triggering a load from disk.

questions.prompt: At which OSI layer does a router primarily operate?
questions.explanation: Routers forward packets based on IP addresses at the Network layer (3); switches operate at layer 2.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the TCP three-way handshake?

options.text: To establish a connection and synchronize sequence numbers

questions.explanation: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK establishes the connection and synchronizes initial sequence numbers before data transfer.

questions.prompt: Which relationship best describes 'a Car HAS-A Engine'?
questions.explanation: HAS-A denotes composition/aggregation; IS-A denotes inheritance.

questions.prompt: Favoring composition over inheritance can reduce tight coupling between classes.
questions.explanation: Composition builds behavior from parts with narrower interfaces, avoiding fragile deep inheritance hierarchies.

questions.prompt: How many bits are in one byte?
questions.explanation: A byte is 8 bits on virtually all modern systems.

questions.prompt: A cache 'hit' means:

options.text: The requested data was found in the cache
Data had to be fetched from RAM

questions.explanation: A hit is when requested data is already in the cache; a miss requires fetching from a lower level.

questions.prompt: What does regression testing verify?

options.text: That new changes did not break existing functionality

questions.explanation: Regression testing re-runs existing tests to ensure recent changes have not broken previously working behavior.

questions.prompt: High cohesion within a module means:

options.text: Its elements are strongly related and focused on one responsibility
It depends on many other modules
It is written in one file

questions.explanation: High cohesion means a module's parts work together toward a single, well-defined purpose — generally desirable.
